Here’s a focused 3‑week peaking block tailored for an intermediate female lifter heading into a powerlifting meet in 21 days. Goal: taper volume, maintain or slightly sharpen intensity, practice singles, and arrive fresh. Assumes last 12 weeks of accumulation are complete and technique is solid. Full gym access.

Global structure
- Frequency: 3–4 lifting days/week (primary lifts + light accessories)
- Intensity: Hold 85–93% in Week 1; sharpen to openers in Week 2; taper to ~60–70% technique work in Meet Week with a light primer
- Volume: Systematically reduced each week (approx. 60–65% of prior in Wk1, 35–45% in Wk2, 15–25% in Meet Week)
- Bar speeds: Prioritize fast concentric, crisp pauses, and command practice
- RPE target: Most work RPE 6–8 in Weeks 1–2; RPE 5–6 Meet Week (except opener practice RPE 7)
- Rest: 3–5 min main sets; 1.5–2.5 min accessories

Meet day attempt strategy (set now; rehearse in Week 2)
- Openers (~90–92% of best recent clean single; RPE 7):
  - Squat: 90–92%
  - Bench: 90–92%
  - Deadlift: 90–92%
- 2nd attempts (~96–98%; RPE 8–8.5)
- 3rd attempts: 100–103% depending on bar speed and calls (RPE 9–9.5)

Week 1: Peak Exposure, Reduced Volume (21–15 days out)
Objective: Exposure to heavy singles (90–93%) with minimal back-off; keep technique sharp, manage fatigue.

Day 1 – Squat Focus
- Competition Squat
  - Work up to 1@90–92% (RPE ~7)
  - Back-off: 2–3 sets x 2 reps @ 82–85% (RPE 7) with full meet commands in your head
- Squat Secondary (technique groove)
  - 2 x 3 @ 70–72% (controlled 2–3 sec eccentric)
- Accessories (light, optional)
  - Single-leg press or split squat: 2 x 8 (easy)
  - Plank: 2 x 45–60s

Day 2 – Bench Volume Taper, Heavy Single
- Competition Bench (pause)
  - 1@90–92% (RPE 7)
  - Back-off: 3 x 2 @ 82–85% (pause 1–2s)
- Close-Grip Bench
  - 2 x 3 @ 75–78% (touch-and-go)
- Upper back/pulling (light)
  - Chest-supported row: 2 x 8–10 easy
  - Band face pulls: 2 x 15–20

Day 3 – Deadlift Focus
- Competition Deadlift (conventional/sumo)
  - 1@90–92% (RPE 7)
  - Back-off: 2 x 2 @ 82–85%
- Deadlift variation (technique)
  - 2 x 3 @ 70–72% (pause at mid-shin or tempo 3–1–X)
- Accessories (minimal)
  - Reverse hyper or back extension: 2 x 10
  - Side plank: 2 x 30–45s/side

Day 4 – Bench Technique + Light Squat (optional 4th day)
- Bench (pause)
  - 3 x 2 @ 78–80% (RPE 6–7)
- Squat (light)
  - 2 x 3 @ 65–70% (move fast)
- Shoulder stability
  - DB lateral raise: 2 x 12
  - Triceps pressdowns: 2 x 12–15

Week 2: Sharpen and Set Openers (14–8 days out)
Objective: Rehearse openers, decrease back-off volume, keep accessories minimal. Final small “over-warm” single at opener range.

Day 1 – Squat Opener Rehearsal
- Competition Squat
  - 1@90–92% (planned opener; RPE 7; full commands)
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 2 @ 78–80%
- Light technique
  - 1–2 x 3 @ 65–70% (clean, fast)
- Accessories
  - Very light single-leg work: 1–2 x 8
  - Easy core: 1–2 sets

Day 2 – Bench Opener Rehearsal
- Competition Bench (pause)
  - 1@90–92% (planned opener; RPE 7)
  - Back-off: 2 x 2 @ 78–80% (strict pauses)
- Optional light bench variation
  - 1–2 x 3 @ 70% (close-grip or feet-up)
- Pulling (easy)
  - 2 x 8 row variation
  - 1–2 x 15 band external rotations

Day 3 – Deadlift Opener Rehearsal
- Competition Deadlift
  - 1@90–92% (planned opener; RPE 7)
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 2 @ 78–80%
- Technique groove
  - 1–2 x 3 @ 65–70% (pause/tempo optional)
- Accessories
  - Reverse hyper/back extension: 1–2 x 8
  - Light hamstring curl: 1–2 x 10

Day 4 – Bench Touch-Up + Optional Light Squat
- Bench (pause)
  - 3 x 1 @ 82–85% (crisp, RPE 6–7)
- Squat (very light)
  - 2 x 2 @ 60–65%
- Shoulder/triceps pump: 1 x 12 each if desired

Notes Week 2
- If any opener feels slower than RPE 7–7.5, adjust down 2.5–5 kg. The goal is certainty, not strain.
- No grinders. Cut sets if bar speed drops.

Week 3: Meet Week Taper (7–0 days out)
Objective: Drastically cut volume, maintain movement patterns, prime CNS mid-week, rest into meet.

Day 1 (Mon, ~5–6 days out) – Competition Lifts Light/Moderate
- Squat: 3 x 1 @ 70% (fast, commands)
- Bench (pause): 3 x 1 @ 70%
- Deadlift: 2 x 1 @ 65–70%
- Accessories: optional band pull-aparts or face pulls 1–2 x 15

Day 2 (Wed, ~3–4 days out) – Primer Singles
- Squat: Work to 1 x 80–85% (RPE 6), then stop
- Bench (pause): Work to 1 x 82–85% (RPE 6–6.5)
- Deadlift: 1–2 singles @ 75–80% (RPE 6)
- No back-off sets. Leave the gym feeling springy.

Day 3 (Fri, ~1–2 days out) – Optional Movement/Bench Touch
- If you recover well from light touches:
  - Bench (pause): 3 x 1 @ 60–65%
  - Squat/Deadlift: skip, or 1 x 1 @ 50–55% if anxiety is high
- Otherwise, rest. Prioritize sleep and mobility.

Meet Day Warm-up and Attempts
- Warm-up timing: start ~60–70 min before first squat
  - Squat: bar x 5–8; 40–45% x 3; 60% x 2; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; opener
  - Bench: bar x 8–10; 40–45% x 5; 60% x 3; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; opener (pauses on all)
  - Deadlift: 40–45% x 3; 60% x 2; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; opener
- Attempts
  - 1st: 90–92% (RPE 7) — must be smoke show
  - 2nd: 96–98% (RPE 8–8.5) — secure a PR total path
  - 3rd: 100–103% based on 2nd speed and confidence

Recovery, fatigue management, and monitoring
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours; consistent schedule; optional 20–30 min nap on heavy days
- Mobility: post-session 5–8 minutes (hips/ankles/upper back); avoid deep static stretching pre-lift
- RPE and bar speed: terminate sets if speed dips >10–12% from first rep on back-offs
- Pain rule: if pain >3/10 or changes movement, stop that lift and switch to light accessories or mobility

Nutrition and weight considerations (general meet-week guidance)
- Weeks 1–2: eat at maintenance to slight surplus (+150–250 kcal), 1.7–2.2 g/kg protein, 3–5 g/kg carbs, fats to balance. Salt food normally.
- Meet week:
  - Keep carbs high and consistent; reduce high-fiber and very fatty meals 24–36 hours pre-meet to avoid GI distress.
  - Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day with electrolytes; avoid over-drinking night before.
  - If making weight:
    - Aim to be within 0.5–1.0% of class by 2–3 days out.
    - Small water and fiber manipulation only (e.g., reduce fibrous veggies 24–36h out, modest evening fluid cut, light breakfast if morning weigh-in). Avoid aggressive dehydration.
  - Post-weigh-in (2-hr):
    - 600–1000 ml electrolyte solution in first 30–45 min.
    - 1–1.5 g/kg carbs from easy sources (rice cakes, bagels, bananas, sports drink, honey), 20–30 g protein, low fat.
    - Sip fluids until urine pale, small carb snacks between attempts as needed.

Technique and command practice
- Use commands on every comp rep in Weeks 1–2.
- Bench: consistent 1–2 sec pause on chest, firm butt/foot contact.
- Squat: consistent depth and stance; hold rack and squat commands mentally.
- Deadlift: lockout and hold 1–2 sec; practice down command.

Contingencies
- If any lift feels unusually heavy in Week 1, cut volume further and shift opener plan down 2.5–5 kg.
- If fatigue lingers into Week 2, drop all back-offs; just hit the single.
- If any ache flares, swap accessories for easy blood flow work only.

This 3-week peak tapers volume while keeping regular exposure to heavy singles, sets clear opener practice, and finishes with a low-fatigue primer so she arrives confident and fresh on meet day.

- Bar speed and path should improve or stay identical with the cue. If not, it’s not helping right now.
- Quick screen: after the 90–92% opener rehearsal, ask RPE and pec/shoulder feel. Any pinchy pec/AC joint sensation? Back the cue off to “shoulders down” only.

Here’s a simple, effective 48-hour pre-meet fueling plan to top off glycogen, keep the gut calm, and arrive well-hydrated without bloat. Adjust portions to body size and weight-class needs. This assumes a same-day, 2-hour weigh-in. If you’re easily under the limit, bias slightly higher carbs/sodium; if you’re tight on weight, use the “making weight” notes.

48–24 hours out (Day −2 to Day −1 morning)
Goals: normalize hydration, increase carbs, keep fiber/fat moderate, steady sodium.
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg total across the day from easy sources
  - Examples: white rice, rice cakes, pasta, potatoes, oatmeal/cream of rice, bagels, fruit, low-fiber cereals, tortillas, sports drink.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg (lean sources to keep fat lower)
  - Examples: chicken, turkey, fish, eggs/egg whites, Greek yogurt, whey.
- Fat: moderate (~0.7–1.0 g/kg) but avoid very heavy/fried meals.
- Fiber: moderate; avoid big salads/legumes/very fibrous veg at dinner.
- Sodium: salt meals to taste; include 1–2 salty items (e.g., broth, salted rice/potatoes, soy sauce, pickles) to support plasma volume.
- Fluids: 30–40 ml/kg/day total with electrolytes in 1–2 bottles (don’t over-chug late at night).
- Caffeine/alcohol: normal or slightly reduced caffeine; avoid alcohol.

Sample Day −2 outline (adjust portions)
- Breakfast: bagel + eggs/egg whites + fruit; 500–600 ml water with electrolytes.
- Snack: Greek yogurt + honey + rice cakes.
- Lunch: chicken + white rice + low-fiber veg (peeled cucumber/cooked carrots) + salt.
- Snack: sports drink or juice + banana.
- Dinner: pasta with lean meat sauce; salted; minimal fibrous veg.
- Evening: 300–500 ml fluids; stop large intakes 1–2 h before bed.

24–12 hours out (Day −1 midday to evening)
Goals: top off carbs, reduce gut residue, avoid bloat.
- Carbs: 5–7 g/kg total across the day, focusing on low-fiber, low-fat.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg from lean/easy-to-digest sources.
- Fat: low to moderate (0.4–0.6 g/kg).
- Fiber: low; choose cooked/peeled produce if any.
- Sodium: keep salting food; include 1 salty drink or broth.
- Fluids: 25–35 ml/kg spread through the day; taper intake slightly after dinner.

Sample Day −1 outline
- Breakfast: cream of rice or oatmeal (not too fibrous) + whey + banana + salt.
- Snack: rice cakes with jam + sports drink.
- Lunch: turkey/white fish + jasmine rice + a little soy sauce.
- Snack: bagel + honey; 300–500 ml electrolyte drink.
- Dinner (earlier/lighter): potatoes or rice + chicken; lightly salted; minimal veg.
- Pre-bed: small carb snack if desired (e.g., rice pudding) + 200–300 ml water.

Morning of meet (0–4 hours pre-lift; after weigh-in if 2-hr weigh-in)
- If weighing in: keep intake minimal beforehand; after weigh-in, rehydrate 600–1000 ml electrolyte in 30–45 min and eat 1–1.5 g/kg carbs, 20–30 g protein, low fat.
- If not cutting: a light breakfast 2–3 h before lifting works (bagel + jam + whey; or rice + eggs/egg whites).

Making weight? Simple, conservative tweaks (24–36 hours out)
- Shift fiber down: use peeled/cooked veg only; avoid beans/bran; choose white rice/pasta, rice cakes, bread.
- Slight fluid taper: keep normal hydration earlier, then reduce large fluid boluses after dinner; sip as needed. Don’t dehydrate aggressively.
- Avoid very salty “new” foods late at night to limit transient water retention. Resume normal sodium right after weigh-in.

Quick sodium guide
- Salt each meal (1/4–1/2 tsp across meals per day, adjusted to taste and climate).
- Include one salty item/day: broth, miso soup, pretzels, sports drink with sodium, soy sauce on rice.
- On meet morning post-weigh-in, prioritize sodium in your rehydration (electrolyte tabs or 1/4–1/2 tsp salt across fluids/foods).

Easy carb menu (low fiber, low fat) to rotate in the last 24–48 h
- Rice (white/jasmine), potatoes, pasta, rice cakes, bagels, tortillas, cream of rice, low-fiber cereal, bananas, applesauce, honey/jam, sports drink.
- Keep fats light: a little olive oil, avocado, or nut butter is fine, but avoid heavy sauces/cheese.

Red flags and adjustments
- If you feel bloated or “puffy,” reduce dinner size and fiber on Day −1 and stop fluids 90 minutes before bed.
- If you wake up thirsty, sip 200–300 ml water with electrolytes; don’t overcorrect with large chugs.
- GI sensitivity? Stick to foods you’ve used in training; avoid new high-sodium packaged snacks if they’ve bothered you before.

Bottom line
- 48–24 h: eat normally but carb-forward with steady sodium and hydration.
- Last 24 h: push carbs a bit more, lower fat/fiber, keep sodium consistent, slightly taper fluids at night.
- After weigh-in: rehydrate with electrolytes, then quick carbs + lean protein. Keep grazing small, frequent, and familiar through the session.

  - Thu: 8–10 min easy walk (reduce stiffness)
  - Fri: optional 8–10 min easy walk if it calms nerves
  - Meet day arrival: 5–7 min relaxed walk/arm swings if helpful

- 48–24 h out:
  - Carbs 4–6 g/kg/day from easy sources (rice, pasta, potatoes, bagels, fruit, low-fiber cereal, sports drink)
  - Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg (lean sources)
  - Fat moderate 0.7–1.0 g/kg
  - Fiber moderate; avoid large fibrous dinners
  - Sodium: salt meals; include 1–2 salty items (broth/soy sauce/pretzels)
  - Fluids: 30–40 ml/kg/day with electrolytes in 1–2 bottles; avoid big late chugs
- 24–12 h out:
  - Carbs 5–7 g/kg/day (low fiber, low fat), Protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg, Fat 0.4–0.6 g/kg, very low fiber late
  - Keep sodium consistent; include one salty drink or broth
  - Fluids 25–35 ml/kg; taper slightly after dinner; small pre-bed snack OK

  - If weighing in: minimal intake before; post-weigh-in 600–1000 ml electrolyte in 30–45 min + 1–1.5 g/kg carbs + 20–30 g protein, low fat

- Sleep: aim 7.5–9 h nightly; naps 20–30 min on heavy/single days
- Mobility: 5–8 min post-session (hips/ankles/T-spine); avoid deep static stretching pre-lift
- Pain rule: if pain >3/10 or alters movement, stop that lift and swap to light blood flow work
- Bar speed guardrail: cut a set if back-off rep speed drops >10–12% vs first rep
- Adjustments:
  - If Week 1 heavies feel unusually hard, trim back-offs and downshift planned opener 2.5–5 kg
  - If 95% single in Week 2 trends ≥RPE 9, stop there and adjust opener downward 2.5–5 kg

This plan integrates the deload, mid-block 95% singles, easy cardio, conservative cueing, and precise nutrition/timing to ensure she peaks cleanly and hits the platform fresh and confident.

Here’s the complete 3-week meet prep program with all adjustments integrated: added deload microcycle between Weeks 1–2, 95% singles in the shifted opener week, easy cardio touches, refined bench cueing approach, meet-day morning plan, and 48-hour pre-meet nutrition guidance. Goal remains: taper volume, hold intensity, rehearse singles/openers, arrive fresh.

Block overview
- Frequency: 3–4 lifting days/week; accessories minimal and easy
- Intensity progression:
  - Week 1: heavy singles 90–92% with limited back-offs
  - Deload Microcycle (3–4 days): 67–75% easy technique work
  - Week 2 (shifted opener week): single at 95% per lift; minimal/no back-offs
  - Meet Week: low-volume touches and primer singles
- Volume taper: ~60–65% of prior in Week 1, ~25–35% in deload, ~35–45% in Week 2 (despite 95% singles), ~15–25% in Meet Week
- RPE: Week 1 mostly 6–8; Deload 5–6; Week 2 top singles 8–8.5 with no grinders; Meet Week 5–6 (primer at 6)
- Rest: 3–5 min on main sets; 1.5–2.5 min light accessories
- Command practice: use meet commands on all comp singles and most warm-ups in Weeks 1–2

Attempt strategy (set in Week 2, rehearse mentally)
- Openers: ~90–92% (RPE ~7) for squat/bench/deadlift
- Seconds: ~96–98% (RPE 8–8.5) adjusted by bar speed
- Thirds: 100–103%+ based on second attempt speed and meet goals

Week 1: Peak exposure, reduced volume (21–15 days out)
Objective: expose to heavy singles (90–92%) with minimal fatigue; groove commands.

Day 1 – Squat focus
- Competition Squat
  - Work to 1 x 90–92% (RPE ~7; full commands)
  - Back-off: 2–3 x 2 @ 82–85% (RPE ~7) OR cut to 1–2 x 2 if fatigue lingers
- Technique groove
  - Squat 2 x 3 @ 70–72% (2–3s controlled eccentric; fast concentric)
- Accessories (optional/easy)
  - Split squat or single-leg press 2 x 8 easy
  - Plank 2 x 45–60s

Day 2 – Bench heavy single, tapering volume
- Competition Bench (all paused)
  - 1 x 90–92% (RPE ~7)
  - Back-off: 3 x 2 @ 82–85% (RPE 7) or 2 x 2 if fatigue shows
- Light bench variation
  - Close-grip 2 x 3 @ 75–78% (touch-and-go, snappy)
- Upper back (light)
  - Chest-supported row 2 x 8–10 easy
  - Band face pulls 2 x 15–20

Day 3 – Deadlift focus
- Competition Deadlift
  - 1 x 90–92% (RPE ~7; clean lockout/hold)
  - Back-off: 2 x 2 @ 82–85%
- Technique variation
  - 2 x 3 @ 70–72% (tempo 3–1–X or 1s pause at mid-shin)
- Accessories (minimal)
  - Reverse hyper or back extension 2 x 10 easy
  - Side plank 2 x 30–45s/side

Day 4 – Optional light day (bench touch + light squat)
- Bench (paused): 3 x 2 @ 78–80% (RPE 6–7)
- Squat (light): 2 x 3 @ 65–70% (move fast)
- Shoulders/triceps: DB laterals 2 x 12; pressdowns 2 x 12–15

Deload Microcycle: 3–4 days between Weeks 1 and 2 (about 14–11 days out)
Objective: shed residual fatigue; keep patterns sharp. Choose 3 sessions across 4 days.

Global rules
- Intensity: 67–75% (cap ~77%) at RPE 5–6
- Volume: 6–10 total working reps per lift per session
- No grinders; cut sets if anything trends >RPE 6

Day A – Squat + light Bench
- Squat: 3 x 2 @ 70–72% (commands in head)
- Bench (pause): 3 x 2 @ 67–70%
- Optional: band face pulls 2 x 15; 8–10 min easy walk

Day B – Bench touch + light Pull
- Bench (pause): 4 x 1 @ 72–75% (crisp pauses)
- Deadlift: 3 x 1 @ 70–72% (smooth lockout/hold)
- Optional: reverse hyper/back extensions 2 x 8 very easy

Day C – Deadlift + light Squat (48h after Day A)
- Deadlift: 2 x 2 @ 70–72%
- Squat: 2 x 2 @ 65–68% (fast, clean depth)
- Optional: plank 2 x 30–45s; 3–4 min breathing (long exhales)

Week 2 (shifted opener week with 95% singles): ~9–6 days out
Objective: confidence-building heavy singles without volume fatigue. One 95% single per lift; minimal or zero back-offs. Space lower-body days by 48+ hours.

Day 1 – Squat 95% single + light bench (≈9–8 days out)
- Squat warm-up progression: bar x 5–8; 40–45% x 3; 60% x 2; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; 90% x 1; 95% x 1 (RPE 8–8.5; full commands)
- Back-off: none, or 1 x 1 @ ~80% only if desired for confidence
- Bench (light technique): 2 x 2 @ 70% paused, fast
- Note: If 95% is slower than expected (≥RPE 9 feel), reduce planned opener 2.5–5 kg and skip any back-offs.

Day 2 – Bench 95% single (≈8–7 days out; 24–36h after Day 1)
- Bench warm-up: bar x 8–10; 40–45% x 5; 60% x 3; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; 90% x 1; 95% x 1 (paused)
- Back-off: none, or 1 x 1 @ ~80% if it feels snappy
- Optional easy upper back: face pulls 1–2 x 15

Day 3 – Deadlift 95% single (≈7–6 days out; 48h after Day 1)
- Deadlift warm-up: 40–45% x 3; 60% x 2; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; 90% x 1; 95% x 1 (hold lockout 1–2s)
- Back-off: none, or 1 x 1 @ ~80% if very crisp
- Optional: 1 x 8–10 very easy reverse hypers or back extensions

Optional Day 4 (only if she recovers fast; otherwise skip)
- 2–3 days after the bench single: Bench 3 x 1 @ 82–85% (RPE 6–7), strict pauses

Meet Week (7–0 days out): taper and prime
Objective: drastically reduced volume, maintain patterns, low-fatigue primer mid-week.

Day 1 (Mon, ~5–6 days out) – Light singles
- Squat: 3 x 1 @ 70% (commands)
- Bench (pause): 3 x 1 @ 70%
- Deadlift: 2 x 1 @ 65–70%
- Optional: band pull-aparts 1–2 x 15

Day 2 (Wed, ~3–4 days out) – Primer singles
- Squat: 1 x 80–85% (RPE ~6) then stop
- Bench (pause): 1 x 82–85% (RPE 6–6.5)
- Deadlift: 1–2 x 75–80% (RPE ~6)
- No back-offs; leave feeling springy

Day 3 (Fri, ~1–2 days out) – Optional light touch
- If she benefits: Bench (pause) 3 x 1 @ 60–65%
- Otherwise rest; emphasize sleep and calm mobility

Competition-day morning flow (2-hr weigh-in assumed)
- T−3:30 to 4:00 h: Wake, 400–600 ml electrolytes sipped, 5–7 min easy walk + gentle mobility + breathing
- Weigh-in (T−2:00 to 1:30): After weigh-in, rehydrate 600–1000 ml electrolyte over 30–45 min; eat 1–1.5 g/kg carbs (bagel, rice cakes, banana, sports drink, honey) + 20–30 g protein; low fat
- T−1:15: Confirm rack heights, equipment, openers; practice commands mentally
- T−1:00: Start squat warm-up
  - Bar x 5–8; 40–45% x 3; 60% x 2; 72–75% x 1; 82–85% x 1; opener
  - Time last warm-up single to finish 6–10 min before first attempt
- Attempts per lift
  - 1st: 90–92% (RPE ~7)
  - 2nd: 96–98% (adjust down to 94–96% if opener slower than expected)
  - 3rd: 100–103% based on 2nd’s speed/confidence
- Between attempts: sit, breathe, 1–2 sips sports drink, small carb bite if desired

Bench cueing during peak/meet
- Keep it simple: one setup cue “pin shoulders to the pad” (depress + retract, not maximal squeeze), one press cue “press back” or “legs then bar”
- Avoid changing grip width/arch or over-squeezing scapulae during descent

Cardio integration (strictly easy; no fatigue)
- Global: RPE 3–4; 55–65% HRmax; 10–20 minutes; separate from heavy lifting by 6–8 hours or place on rest days
- Week 1:
  - Day 0 (before Week 1 starts): 15–20 min easy bike + 3–5 min relaxed breathing
  - Day 2 (bench day): 10–12 min easy spin after or later that day
  - Day 4 (optional light day): 12–15 min easy walk
  - Optional: 10 min very easy walk the morning after deadlifts
- Deload Microcycle: 1–2 sessions of 10–12 min easy bike/walk; skip if legs feel heavy
- Week 2 (95% singles): Max one 10–12 min easy session post-bench day only
- Meet Week:
  - Mon: 10–12 min easy bike after light singles (strictly easy)
  - Thu: 8–10 min easy walk (reduce stiffness)
  - Fri: optional 8–10 min easy walk if it calms nerves
  - Meet day arrival: 5–7 min relaxed walk/arm swings if helpful

48-hour pre-meet nutrition (2-hr weigh-in)
- 48–24 h out:
  - Carbs 4–6 g/kg/day from easy sources (rice, pasta, potatoes, bagels, fruit, low-fiber cereal, sports drink)
  - Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg (lean sources)
  - Fat moderate 0.7–1.0 g/kg
  - Fiber moderate; avoid large fibrous dinners
  - Sodium: salt meals; include 1–2 salty items (broth/soy sauce/pretzels)
  - Fluids: 30–40 ml/kg/day with electrolytes in 1–2 bottles; avoid big late chugs
- 24–12 h out:
  - Carbs 5–7 g/kg/day (low fiber, low fat), Protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg, Fat 0.4–0.6 g/kg, very low fiber late
  - Keep sodium consistent; include one salty drink or broth
  - Fluids 25–35 ml/kg; taper slightly after dinner; small pre-bed snack OK
- Morning of meet:
  - If weighing in: minimal intake before; post-weigh-in 600–1000 ml electrolyte in 30–45 min + 1–1.5 g/kg carbs + 20–30 g protein, low fat
  - If not cutting: light breakfast 2–3 h pre-lift (bagel + jam + whey or rice + egg whites)

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: aim 7.5–9 h nightly; naps 20–30 min on heavy/single days
- Mobility: 5–8 min post-session (hips/ankles/T-spine); avoid deep static stretching pre-lift
- Pain rule: if pain >3/10 or alters movement, stop that lift and swap to light blood flow work
- Bar speed guardrail: cut a set if back-off rep speed drops >10–12% vs first rep
- Adjustments:
  - If Week 1 heavies feel unusually hard, trim back-offs and downshift planned opener 2.5–5 kg
  - If 95% single in Week 2 trends ≥RPE 9, stop there and adjust opener downward 2.5–5 kg

This plan integrates the deload, mid-block 95% singles, easy cardio, conservative cueing, and precise nutrition/timing to ensure she peaks cleanly and hits the platform fresh and confident.
